stances.claim: The Comelec Precinct Finder is unreliable, returns false 'NO RECORD FOUND' results to legitimately registered voters, and should be withdrawn immediately until properly tested.
stances.rhetorical_move: personal-testimony-as-evidence (CJ's own 'NO RECORD FOUND' screenshot) combined with class-affected framing (hundreds of voters and 4.1M new young voters)

stances.claim: Statutorily-mandated alternatives -- the 90-day posted list under RA 8189, the polling-place posting, the PPCRV copy, and the EDCVL in Electoral Boards' custody -- already provide reliable means of verifying voter registration without the digital Precinct Finder.
stances.rhetorical_move: statutory-hierarchy framing (the law already provides better tools than this gimmick)

stances.claim: The EDCVL is the prima facie authority -- appearing in the Precinct Finder or any other list is insufficient if the voter's name is not on the EDCVL on Election Day.
stances.rhetorical_move: legal-hierarchy clarification (educating readers on what actually controls)

stances.claim: The VIS hand-out received by CJ's household put 'to terrible shame' the Precinct Finder -- Comelec's own paper alternative under RA 7904 is more reliable than its online tool.
stances.rhetorical_move: embarrassment-by-comparison (Comelec already produces a better artifact)
stances.confidence: asserted with concrete VIS contents reproduced

stances.claim: Digital tools 'should be thoroughly tested before they are inflicted on the public' -- a generalizable principle for election technology.
stances.rhetorical_move: principle-generalization (move from one defective tool to a category rule)

notable_anecdotes: CJ personally accessed voterverifier.comelec.gov.ph and got 'NO RECORD FOUND' -- took a cellphone photo of the screen and was 'horrified' that he, a former Chief Justice who has voted in every past election, was apparently disenfranchised.

He engaged election lawyer Romulo Macalintal and authorized use of the photo in Macalintal's press conference the very same morning -- turning his personal screenshot into public-interest evidence on behalf of hundreds of similarly-affected voters.

Macalintal then obtained the physical 'List of Voters' from Comelec showing CJ and his wife Leni properly listed in Precinct 0205A, Makati -- proof the registration existed and the Precinct Finder, not the registration, was at fault.

While CJ was still drafting the column, a 'Voter Information Sheet' hand-out arrived at his household with his name, address ('PANGANIBAN, ARTEMIO VILLASENOR'), Precinct No. 0205A/CP# 75, and voting center Dasmariñas Clubhouse, Campanilla St. -- the timing dramatized that Comelec already has a working paper system that shames its own digital one.
Sharp rhetorical pivot: Comelec should 'expurgate' the Precinct Finder 'like it unabashedly purges nuisance candidates' -- turning Comelec's own term for vetting against its defective tool.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with the indignation of a former Chief Justice who, checking his own precinct via the Comelec's online 'Precinct Finder' at voterverifier.comelec.gov.ph, was met with 'NO RECORD FOUND' -- a result he photographed on his cellphone and turned over to election lawyer Romulo Macalintal, who used it in a press conference that morning on behalf of hundreds of similarly-affected voters. Macalintal then secured the physical 'List of Voters' confirming CJ and his wife Leni were properly registered in Precinct 0205A, Makati -- proving the registration existed and the tool was the failure. Looking deeper, CJ walks readers through the statutorily-mandated alternatives under RA 8189 (the 90-day posted list at the Office of the Election Registrar and LGU bulletin boards), the Election Day postings at polling places, the PPCRV copy, and most importantly the Election Day Computerized Voters List (EDCVL) which is the prima facie authority on who may vote in a specific precinct. As he wrote, a 'Voter Information Sheet' arrived at his household under RA 7904 with all the correct details -- putting 'to terrible shame' the digital Precinct Finder. He calls on Comelec to 'expurgate' the unreliable tool 'like it unabashedly purges nuisance candidates,' restore it only after thorough testing, and closes with the generalizable principle that hi-tech and digital apps 'should be thoroughly tested before they are inflicted on the public.'
